prompt:
```xml
<message name="IDS_FOO_TITLE" desc="Title for the Foo settings section"
         translateable="true">
  Foo
</message>
```

What should the reviewer say about this `.grdp` entry?
choices: Good — always mark strings explicitly translateable so the tooling picks them up
Change it to `translatable="true"` (correct spelling)
Remove it — `translateable="true"` is the default
Replace it with `translateable="false"` for settings titles
explain: `translateable="true"` is the default in GRD/GRDP files, so never add it explicitly. Only `translateable="false"` is meaningful to the tooling.

prompt: Which menu-item string follows Brave's UI text conventions?
choices: `Save page as...`
`Save page as . . .`
`Save page as`
`Save page as…`
explain: Use the proper Unicode ellipsis character `…` instead of three periods `...` in user-facing strings.

prompt: Which `desc` best serves translators for a string whose text is just "History"?
choices: `desc="History"`
`desc="Title for the browser visits history section of a URL picker"`
`desc="History text shown in the URL picker, translate as appropriate"`
`desc=""` (left empty since the text is self-explanatory)
explain: Translators often see only the description, so add context: the UI element type and disambiguation (browser vs. conversation history). Never leave `desc` empty — though for truly self-evident strings like "Cancel", a brief description is fine.

prompt: A reviewer insists a `Cancel` button string needs a three-sentence description. Another string uses the same copy-pasted `desc` as an unrelated tooltip. Which feedback is valid?
choices: Only the copy-pasted `desc` needs fixing
Both are fine; descriptions are optional as long as the string text is clear
Both need fixing: every `desc` must be several sentences
Only the `Cancel` one needs fixing; reusing descriptions is encouraged
explain: Each description must be unique to its purpose, specify the UI element type, and be proofread. But don't insist on verbose descriptions for strings that speak for themselves.

prompt: In a new Lit-based WebUI component, how should localized strings be accessed?
choices: Call `loadTimeData.getString()` directly in `render()`
Hardcode English and let the build translate it
Use `I18nMixinLit`
Fetch strings over a mojo call at startup
explain: In Lit WebUI components, use `I18nMixinLit` instead of calling `loadTimeData.getString()` directly — it's the standard, consistent i18n approach.

prompt: You need to change the wording of an upstream string defined in `app/generated_resources.grd`. What's the correct approach?
choices: Edit the text directly in `app/generated_resources.grd`
Patch `app/generated_resources.grd` and regenerate with `pnpm run update_patches`
Edit each locale's `.xtb` file with the new translation
Add a Brave string and redirect the upstream `IDS_` via chromium_src
explain: Never modify upstream GRD/GRDP files — they're replaced on every Chromium bump. Add the string to the Brave GRD/GRDP and redirect the upstream `IDS_` constant via a chromium_src `#undef`/`#define`.

prompt: Brave needs a simple word substitution applied across many upstream strings in all locales. What's the recommended tool?
choices: `grd_string_replacements.py` with `default_replacements`
A chromium_src `#undef`/`#define` override for each affected `IDS_` constant
Manually edit each upstream GRD file and all its `.xtb` translations
A runtime string replace in `l10n_util::GetStringUTF16`
explain: For simple word/phrase substitutions across upstream strings, use `brave/script/lib/l10n/grd_string_replacements.py` with `default_replacements` and `pnpm run chromium_rebase_l10n` — it applies consistently across all locales.

prompt: You add a string to the AI Chat WebUI GRDP file, whose WebUI component is `AiChat`. Which attribute is correct?
choices: `formatter_data="webui=AIChat"`
`formatter_data="webui=AiChat"`
`formatter_data="webui=ai_chat"`
No `formatter_data` — the build infers it from the file path
explain: WebUI GRDP strings need `formatter_data="webui=ComponentName"` that exactly matches the WebUI component identifier; a typo or mismatch means the string won't be in that bundle.

prompt: Which placeholder follows the GRD/GRDP standard?
choices: `<ph name="SITE_NAME">$1<ex>example.com</ex></ph>`
`<ph name="PH_1">$1</ph>`
`<ph name="siteName">$1<ex>example.com</ex></ph>`
`<ph name="SITE_NAME">$1</ph>` (examples are optional)
explain: Placeholders need descriptive SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE names and an `<ex>` example showing translators the runtime value. Use `LINK_BEGIN`/`LINK_END` for link placeholders.

prompt: A settings group has two sibling toggle labels: "Background Image" and "Brave backgrounds". What's the reviewer's feedback?
choices: Fine — each string can choose its own capitalization based on its own content
Both should be all lowercase for a modern look
Only the first word of a label may ever be capitalized
Same level, mixed title and sentence case; make them consistent
explain: Strings within a feature or UI surface must use consistent capitalization. Title case is for page titles, section headers, buttons, and menu items; sentence case for descriptions, body text, tooltips, and helper text.

prompt: Which string follows Brave's UI text conventions?
choices: "Sync bookmarks, passwords, etc. with Shields on"
"Sync our bookmarks, passwords, and more with Shields on"
"Sync bookmarks, passwords, and more with Shields up"
"Sync bookmarks, passwords, etc. with Shields up"
explain: Use "and more" instead of "etc.", "Brave's" instead of "our", and match established feature vocabulary (Shields are "up/down", not "on/off").

prompt: Which description is better for a button that shares open tabs with the AI assistant?
choices: "Send your tabs' contents"
"Send the content of your tabs to Brave AI"
"Send your tabs"
"Send our tabs' contents to our AI assistant"
explain: Be explicit about data-sharing actions (say where data goes), avoid possessive constructions like "tabs' contents" for translatability, and use "Brave" rather than "our".

prompt: A PR adds five new `IDS_` strings to a GRDP "for an upcoming follow-up", but none are referenced in code yet. What should the reviewer say?
choices: Fine — adding strings early gives translators a head start before the feature lands
Fine, as long as they're marked `translateable="true"`
Remove them until code references them; every string goes to translation
Keep them but give them empty descriptions
explain: Only add GRD/GRDP strings that are actively referenced in the codebase, and remove strings that become unused. Reviewers should verify each `IDS_` constant is actually used.

prompt: After a Chromium rebase, new upstream strings mention "Google Pay" and "Gemini". What's expected?
choices: Review them and replace Google product names with Brave branding
Leave them — upstream strings are never shown in Brave
Replace "Google Pay" with "Brave Wallet" everywhere it appears in the new strings
Wait for users to report the branding issue
explain: During rebases, review new upstream strings for Google product names and ensure correct Brave branding. Note "Brave Wallet" means the crypto wallet only — not general autofill/payment cards.

choices: Template literals are slower than string concatenation
It should use `toLowerCase()` to match key conventions
Nothing, provided every model key has a matching string defined in the GRDP
It defeats static analysis and dead-string detection
explain: Never construct `getLocale()` keys dynamically — it defeats static analysis, prevents dead string detection, and breaks if key formats change. Use explicit keys like `S.CHAT_UI_CLAUDE_SUBTITLE`, or have the data source provide the string.

prompt:
```cpp
html_source->AddString(
    "sectionDescription",
    l10n_util::GetStringFUTF16(IDS_SECTION_DESCRIPTION, kLearnMoreURL));
```

What's the recommended alternative?
choices: Embed the full `<a href>` markup into the GRD string itself so translators see it
Pass the URL as a separate string; build the link in the UI
Keep it, but escape the URL with `base::EscapeForHTML`
Hardcode the URL into each locale's translation
explain: Build links in the UI, not in localized strings. Pass the URL separately (via `AddString` or a mojom constant) instead of formatting it into the localized string in C++.

prompt: Which settings toggle description is punctuated correctly?
choices: "Block trackers on all sites." (single sentence, with period)
"Block trackers on all sites" (single sentence, no period)
"Block trackers on all sites. This may break some sites" (no final period)
"Block trackers on all sites!" (exclamation)
explain: Single-sentence toggle descriptions don't end with a period; multi-sentence descriptions do end with a period on the last sentence.

prompt: A string reviewer sees: "Some extensions are non compatible on this page and". What should they flag?
choices: Nothing — translators will clean up the grammar in each language anyway
Only that it should be in title case
It's truncated, and "non compatible" needs a hyphen
Only that it should end with an ellipsis
explain: Strings must be complete, grammatically correct, and properly punctuated — no truncated sentences, hyphenated compound adjectives, and appropriate prepositions — since translators use the English source as reference.

prompt: Your PR adds three new user-facing strings to a dialog. What should you include for string review?
choices: A screenshot attached as an inline code review comment
Just the GRDP diff — it shows the exact text
A link to the design mock instead of the real UI
A screenshot of the rendered UI in the PR description
explain: When adding or modifying user-facing strings, include a screenshot of the actual rendered UI in the PR description (not inline comments) so reviewers can check truncation, capitalization, layout, and terminology.
